newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 lower Tuesday on the heels of a weak performance in London overnight, dealers said.
LIFFE cocoa futures erased early gains and traded lower at midday Wednesday. Benchmark July fell 12 stg at the break to 989 stg per tonne, while May slipped 10 stg to 965 stg.

Tuesday, New York cocoa futures tumbled to eight-week lows, pounded by technically inspired speculative selling. July cocoa closed down $40 at $1,414 a tonne after trading from $1,466 to $1,397. Spot May ended down $34, to $1,408, while the back months closed $37 to $41 lower.
On the charts, traders pegged nearby July support at $1,400, with a solid downside target noted at $1,360. Resistance was seen at $1,440.

Fundamentally, broker GNI cut its 1996/97 world cocoa deficit estimate to 33,000 tonnes from its earlier forecast of 180,000 tonnes due to an increased production projection for top-grower Ivory Coast.
"We would not even rule out a marginal surplus if the (Ivorian) mid-crop comes in as large as some traders are predicting," GNI said in its daily commentary.
GNI put total 1996/97 Ivorian output at 1.15 million tonnes, including a 160,000-tonne mid-crop.
In other news, official shipping data in the Ivory Coast showed the country's cocoa bean exports jumped to 171,104 tonnes in March, against 148,827 in February and 169,065 in March 1996.
Ivorian semi-finished cocoa product and powder exports fell to 6,530 tonnes in March from 8,830 tonnes in February, shipping data showed.
